## Design

### 2026-11-01: I first spent about 2.75 hours (The additional amount listed) researching and learning how a projector functions, as well as planning how it would. I decided that for my LCD projector, I would try to

**4.08h**

I first spent about 2.75 hours (The additional amount listed) researching and learning how a projector functions, as well as planning how it would. I decided that for my LCD projector, I would try to use a 3D printer replacement screen as the LCD panel, as they usually come cheap for their resolution. I decided to attempt for 1440p at a 5.5 inch panel.The backlight would be powered on its own and I would use a PC grade heatsink to cool it. For the case, it will simply house the other parts and possibly feature a dial connect to a rack and pinion to move the LCD panel, to allow to focus at different distances from a wall. I will try to make it as compact as possible but it may be difficult. There would be a heat isolation glass between the backlight and projector to prevent it from getting damaged. Next, I began shopping for parts to find a good LCD panel that was under a thousand dollars, as well as a size that would be usable without making an enourmous build. I also made a pcb to control the backlight and the heatsink (because 100W gets hot) and it will be controlled by an Arduino nano.  I was making sure to take screenshots every once in a while, because I have seen on slack that  videos corrupt sometimes (fortunately mine didn't so I was ok). I don't know if its counted in this entry but I made the code for the arduino shortly after finishing the PCB. I am new to C++, but it was not as different from Java as I originally thought, so writing the code was not too difficult (with a little translation of syntax from google). I will probably be funding the project myself since the parts get pretty expensive, and my next goal is to CAD a 3d printed case.

### 2026-11-01: I made the CAD for my projector case (3d printed) that will house all of the components. I decided to try using a type of ratchet like mechanism for the focus because I don't know how to make accurate

**1.42h**

I made the CAD for my projector case (3d printed) that will house all of the components. I decided to try using a type of ratchet like mechanism for the focus because I don't know how to make accurate gears in fusion so I didn't want to learn just for one rack and pinion. For most of the parts that don't have clear screw holes, I plan to just use a hand drill and create a tapped hole for them in the case (I will use inserts to thread them properly). It took me about 30 minutes to plan that out but I feel like it will be good because I don't have to worry as much about tolerances.
